name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER10_DIAG_Q01 - Maturation of proinsulin into mature active insulin

questiontext.text:
The diagram below illustrates the post-translational processing and maturation of mammalian proinsulin into functional insulin:

Identify the polypeptide chains designated as Chain X, Chain Y, and the excised segment Peptide Z:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The diagram illustrates the prohormone proinsulin undergoing proteolytic processing to yield mature insulin and a free released peptide segment. Three distinct peptide components are labelled: Chain X (blue upper strand), Chain Y (green lower strand), and Peptide Z (dashed connecting loop).

Step 2: Biological Principles of Insulin Biosynthesis
Mammalian insulin is initially translated as an inactive single-chain prohormone containing three distinct polypeptide segments arranged from amino to carboxy terminus: Chain B, connecting C peptide, and Chain A. Interchain disulfide bridges form between specific cysteine residues linking Chain A and Chain B.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
During post-translational maturation within secretory granules, endopeptidases cleave the connecting C peptide. In standard textbook representations, mature insulin consists of the A peptide (21 amino acids) and the B peptide (30 amino acids) covalently stabilized by disulfide bonds, while the free C peptide is released as a byproduct.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working and Identification
Chain X represents the A peptide (21 amino acids), Chain Y represents the B peptide (30 amino acids), and the excised connecting loop Z represents the C peptide.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Verifying with mammalian proinsulin maturation, mature active insulin contains only chains A and B linked by disulfide bridges, whereas the C peptide is entirely excised. Thus, Chain X is the A peptide, Chain Y is the B peptide, and Peptide Z is the C peptide.

answer.text: Chain X = A peptide; Chain Y = B peptide; Peptide Z = C peptide
Chain X = B peptide; Chain Y = A peptide; Peptide Z = Signal peptide
Chain X = C peptide; Chain Y = A peptide; Peptide Z = B peptide
Chain X = A peptide; Chain Y = C peptide; Peptide Z = B peptide

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER10_DIAG_Q02 - Cotton boll damage and resistance conferred by Bt toxin

questiontext.text:
Examine the schematic representation of two cotton bolls harvested from different plants:

Which genetic introduction from Bacillus thuringiensis protects cotton boll (Q) from destruction by cotton bollworms?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The diagram contrasts two cotton bolls: Boll (P) is bored into, perforated, and destroyed by larvae of the cotton bollworm, whereas Boll (Q) is fully mature with intact white lint harvested from a transgenic insect-resistant plant.

Step 2: Biological Principles of Bt Cotton
Cotton bollworms are lepidopteran insect pests whose larvae feed on and destroy cotton bolls. Transgenic Bt cotton is engineered by cloning insect-group specific crystalline endotoxin genes from the bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis into the plant genome.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Gene Assignments
According to established molecular biology principles, the specific genes controlling cotton bollworms are cryIAc and cryIIAb. In contrast, the gene cryIAb controls the European corn borer.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working and Evaluation
To confer resistance against cotton bollworms and produce the healthy phenotype observed in boll (Q), recombinant plants must express the proteins encoded by cryIAc and cryIIAb.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Verifying specific target assignments, genes cryIAc and cryIIAb are designated specifically for cotton bollworm protection. Hence, the correct genetic introduction consists of the proteins encoded by genes cryIAc and cryIIAb.

answer.text: Expression of cryIAc and cryIIAb genes controlling cotton bollworms
Synthesis of single-stranded antisense DNA degrading bollworm ribosomes

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER10_DIAG_Q03 - Host plant-mediated RNAi protection against root nematode

questiontext.text:
The diagram below depicts the phenotypes of tobacco root systems following challenge with the root-knot nematode Meloidogyne incognita:

What cellular process was engineered into the transgenic host to achieve this protection against Meloidogyne incognita?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The diagram illustrates two tobacco root systems exposed to the nematode Meloidogyne incognita. The control roots exhibit extensive tumor-like galls (root knots) causing tissue destruction, whereas the transgenic roots exhibit normal, healthy, gall-free fibrous root development.

Step 2: Biological Principles of RNA Interference (RNAi)
RNA interference is a post-transcriptional gene silencing mechanism universal to eukaryotic cells. When introduced into a host plant via Agrobacterium vectors, nematode-specific DNA sequences are transcribed to produce both sense and anti-sense RNA.

Step 3: Relevant Principles and Interaction Cascade
The complementary sense and anti-sense RNA strands anneal to form double-stranded RNA (dsRNA). When the parasitic nematode ingests cell sap containing this dsRNA, host-initiated RNAi triggers sequence-specific cleavage and degradation of the parasite's vital mRNA, preventing its translation and arresting parasite survival.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working and Evaluation
The prevention of gall formation in the transgenic plant is directly mediated by host-generated dsRNA initiating RNAi that silences nematode mRNA, preventing the parasite from establishing infection in the host roots.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Reviewing the mechanism of protection against Meloidogyne incognita, the responsible strategy is double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) mediated RNA interference (RNAi) that silences specific parasitic mRNA.

answer.text: Direct cleavage of nematode genomic DNA by plant bacterial endonucleases
Silencing of specific nematode mRNA triggered by host plant-generated dsRNA (RNAi)
Secretion of insecticidal Cry protoxin crystals that lyse nematode intestinal cells

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_CHAPTER10_DIAG_Q04 - In vivo pathway of Bt protoxin activation and insect gut lysis

questiontext.text:
The flow diagram below depicts the sequential physiological stages in the lethal action of Bt toxin inside a susceptible insect larva:

Which physiological factor represents Condition [M] and which tissue constitutes Target Cells [N]?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The sequential pathway traces the mode of action of Bt toxin: inactive protein crystals are ingested, solubilized by Condition [M], bind to Target Cells [N], and cause transmembrane pore formation, cell swelling, lysis, and death.

Step 2: Biological Principles of Bt Toxin Activation
Bt toxin crystals remain insoluble and non-toxic until they encounter an alkaline environment. The midgut of susceptible insect larvae possesses an alkaline pH (often pH 9 to 11), which solubilizes the protein crystal, allowing digestive enzymes to cleave the protoxin into its active lytic form.

Step 3: Identification of Target Receptors and Cells
Once activated, the insecticidal Cry toxin binds specifically to surface protein receptors localized exclusively on the apical membrane of midgut epithelial cells.

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working and Evaluation
Condition [M] is the alkaline pH of the insect gut, which solubilizes the protein crystals. Target Cells [N] are the midgut epithelial cells, where pore formation leads to osmotic lysis.

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Condition [M] corresponds to the alkaline pH of the gut, and Target Cells [N] correspond to midgut epithelial cells. Thus, the correct pair is Condition [M] = Alkaline pH of the gut, Target Cells [N] = Midgut epithelial cells.

answer.text: Condition [M] = Acidic pH of the foregut; Target Cells [N] = Hindgut cuticular lining
Condition [M] = Neutral pH of the hemolymph; Target Cells [N] = Malpighian tubules
Condition [M] = Acidic pH of salivary secretions; Target Cells [N] = Tracheal epithelial cells
Condition [M] = Alkaline pH of the gut; Target Cells [N] = Midgut epithelial cells
